statements.text: County and district courts share original jurisdiction in covered civil actions where the debt, damages or value of claimed personal property is $25,000 or less. The county court also has jurisdiction of counterclaims in those actions when the counterclaim does not exceed $25,000.

source.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes 2024, § 13-6-104(1)

statements.text: C.R.C.P. 8 governs the pleading requirements for a district court civil complaint.

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 8

statements.text: JDF 601 is the fillable District Court Civil Case Cover Sheet that accompanies an initial pleading when C.R.C.P. 16.1 requires it.

source.citation: JDF 601 District Court Civil Case Cover Sheet

statements.text: JDF 600 is the official fillable District Court Civil Summons for initial service of process.

source.citation: JDF 600 District Court Civil Summons

statements.text: C.R.S. § 13-32-101(1)(d) governs the current district civil docket fee.

source.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes 2024, § 13-32-101(1)(d)

statements.text: A district court filing fee waiver is requested by motion with a supporting financial affidavit on the Colorado Judicial Branch's fee-waiver forms.

source.citation: Colorado Judicial Branch, district civil fee-waiver motion and financial affidavit

statements.text: Service of process is to be made within 63 days after the complaint is filed (C.R.C.P. 4).

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 4

statements.text: The return or other proof of service is filed with the court after service of process (C.R.C.P. 4).

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 4

statements.text: Colorado Courts E-Filing is a filing channel for eligible self-represented litigants and filings accepted under C.R.C.P. 121 § 1-26.

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 121, § 1-26

statements.text: A district civil answer is due 21 days after in-state service or 35 days after out-of-state service (C.R.C.P. 12).

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 12

statements.text: Under § 13-6-104(1), the county court has concurrent original jurisdiction with the district court in civil actions in which the debt, damage or value of the personal property claimed does not exceed $25,000. The section states no district court monetary ceiling. Whether such a ceiling exists remains unverified.

source.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes 2024, § 13-6-104(1)

statements.text: C.R.C.P. 98 governs the county of venue in a Colorado civil action. Potential grounds include where a defendant resides, works or does business and where a claim arose, such as where a contract was made or a tort occurred. The venue inquiry can include an entity's principal place of business or registered agent, the location of a home office, and the rules for multiple defendants or particular claims.

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 98

statements.text: A pleading may be amended once as of right before a responsive pleading is served. If no responsive pleading is required, the amendment period is 21 days after service of the pleading (C.R.C.P. 15).

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 15

statements.text: A pre-answer motion under C.R.C.P. 12 extends the time to answer until the court decides the motion.

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 12

statements.text: The case caption identifies the court and its mailing address and the parties on the left. The case number, division number and courtroom number appear on the right.

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 10(d)(2)(III)

statements.text: The 2024 statute sets the district civil docket fee at $235 for each plaintiff, petitioner, third-party plaintiff or party filing a crossclaim or counterclaim within the scope of subsection (1).

source.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes 2024, § 13-32-101(1)(d)

statements.text: Electronic filing is required in most Colorado judicial districts (C.R.C.P. 121 § 1-26).

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 121, § 1-26

statements.text: In district civil cases, the case management order typically follows the answer.

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 26(d)

statements.text: C.R.C.P. 4 provides for personal service by a process server or sheriff and service on an entity's registered agent. Certified mail with a signed return receipt is available where authorized. Publication is a last resort and requires court approval.

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 4

statements.text: A responsive brief is due 21 days after the motion is filed, or 14 days after filing if the motion is filed 42 days or less before the trial date, unless the court allows a greater or lesser time.

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 121, § 1-15(1)(b)

statements.text: The moving party has 7 days after the filing of the responsive brief to file a reply brief, or 14 days after that filing for a Rule 56 motion, unless the court allows a greater or lesser time.

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 121, § 1-15(1)(c)

statements.text: Before filing a motion, moving counsel and self-represented parties must confer with opposing counsel and self-represented parties unless a governing statute or rule permits filing without notice. There are exceptions to the duty for self-represented parties to confer and the duty to confer with them. They are for any incarcerated person and any self-represented party as to whom the requirement is contrary to court order or statute, including a protection or restraining order. The motion opens with a good-faith conferral certification. If no conference has occurred, the motion states why, including all efforts to confer. If the relief sought by the motion has been agreed to by the parties or will not be opposed, the court shall be so advised in the motion.

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 121, § 1-15(8)

statements.text: C.R.C.P. 98 governs transfer of a Colorado civil action for improper county or for the convenience of parties or witnesses.

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 98

statements.text: C.R.E. 408 governs the treatment of settlement communications as evidence.

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Evidence, Rule 408

statements.text: Discovery before service of the case management order is barred unless the rules, a court order or party agreement authorizes it. Discovery conducted before issuance of the order shall not exceed the limitations established by Rule 26(b)(2). Methods of discovery may be used in any sequence, and one party's discovery shall not delay any other party's discovery, unless the parties stipulate or the court, upon motion, orders otherwise for the convenience of parties and witnesses and in the interests of justice.

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 26(d)

statements.text: Answers and objections to interrogatories are due within 35 days after service of the interrogatories; the court may direct a shorter or longer time or, in the absence of such an order, the parties may agree to one in writing under C.R.C.P. 29 (Rule 33(b)(3)). A written response to a request for production is due within 35 days after service of the request; the court may direct, or the parties may agree in writing under C.R.C.P. 29 to, a shorter or longer time (Rule 34(b)). A matter in a request for admission is admitted unless, within 35 days after service of the request or such shorter or longer time as the court may allow or the parties may agree to in writing under C.R.C.P. 29, the party to whom the request is directed serves upon the party requesting the admission a written answer or objection addressed to the matter, signed by the party or by the party's attorney (Rule 36(a)).

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rules 33(b)(3), 34(b) and 36(a), in Colorado Revised Statutes 2023, court rules volume

statements.text: A judge may allow a person to commence and prosecute or defend a civil action or special proceeding without paying costs if satisfied that the person is unable to prosecute or defend because the person is poor and unable to pay the costs and expenses. If the person prosecutes or defends successfully, a judgment is entered in the person's favor for the amount of court costs the person would have incurred. That judgment is first satisfied out of any money paid into court, and the costs are paid to the court before the judgment is satisfied of record.

source.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes 2024, § 13-16-103(1)

statements.text: Colorado Courts E-Filing accepts district civil docket-fee payments and fee-waiver submissions (C.R.C.P. 121 § 1-26).

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 121, § 1-26

statements.text: Courts of record may declare rights, status and other legal relations within their respective jurisdictions whether or not further relief is or could be claimed. No action or proceeding shall be open to objection on the ground that a declaratory judgment or decree is prayed for. A declaration may be affirmative or negative and has the force and effect of a final judgment or decree.

source.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes 2024, § 13-51-105

statements.text: C.R.C.P. 57 governs the procedure and form for seeking declaratory relief.

source.citation: Colorado Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 57

obtain: any case management or other order entered in the case
